notes: What each legal instrument mapped on a block can and cannot govern for harvest, replanting, roads and grazing, as read from the primary texts on the date above. A screen, not a legal determination: every cell cites the provision it rests on, and a cell whose answer depends on terms that are not public is 'unknown', naming the document that decides. Layers are read by each footprint part's own polygon (or its convex hull, for a layer of a few very detailed polygons); areas are clipped to the footprint, and lines and points are measured inside it and within the layer's stated margin. Fields are listed narrowly and never include a holder's, client's, owner's or applicant's name or an IDIR user; DataBC returns a layer's mandatory attributes whatever propertyName asks, so the reader keeps only the fields listed here. A context layer names no instrument and has no reach cell: it is read only for what lies under a block (the visual quality page's land status checks), and says why it has no cells.

binds.note: The order reserves Crown land from disposition under the Land Act. A Forest Act agreement to harvest Crown timber is not a Land Act disposition: the Act's dispositions are sales, leases, rights of way or easements, licences to occupy and fossil rights, and agreements to harvest Crown timber are kept out of the Crown land registry. Decision-makers consider the reserve; it does not itself regulate forest work unless the order's terms do. This is a reading of the Act's text; no court decision on the point was found.

harvest.note: The reserve withdraws land from Land Act disposition only, which on this reading does not bar a Forest Act harvest. The order may carry terms and conditions, and only the order in council says whether they reach timber harvesting. This is a reading of the Act's text; no court decision on the point was found.

replant.note: The order's terms decide whether planting is compatible with the reserve's purpose. The free-growing duty is FRPA's, and the reserve does not lift it.

roads.note: A forest service road is kept out of the Crown land registry like a timber agreement, and a reserve does not prevent a Land Act licence to occupy for a road over it. The order's terms decide whether a road is compatible.

grazing.note: Range Act grazing and hay agreements are kept out of the Crown land registry, and the Range Act's Crown range excludes only land leased under the Land Act, so a Range Act agreement can cover reserved land. The order's terms decide whether grazing is compatible.

terms.where: The order in council that made the reserve, and the Crown lands file
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship (Crown land administration)
terms.channel: FrontCounter BC, quoting the Crown lands file number
terms.ask: A copy of the order in council establishing the reserve, with any terms and conditions on the use of the land, and the reserve's purpose and effective date

binds.note: The minister temporarily withdraws Crown land from disposition under the Land Act, and may then refuse an application for it. A Forest Act agreement to harvest Crown timber is not a Land Act disposition. Decision-makers consider the withdrawal; it does not itself regulate forest work unless its terms do. This is a reading of the Act's text; no court decision on the point was found.

harvest.note: The withdrawal is from Land Act disposition only, which on this reading does not bar a Forest Act harvest. The minister may impose terms and conditions on the use of withdrawn land, and only the withdrawal's own record says whether any reach timber harvesting. This is a reading of the Act's text; no court decision on the point was found.

replant.note: Terms on the use of the withdrawn land decide whether planting is compatible. The free-growing duty is FRPA's, and the withdrawal does not lift it.

roads.note: A forest service road is kept out of the Crown land registry like a timber agreement. Terms on the use of the withdrawn land decide whether a road is compatible.

grazing.note: A Range Act agreement can cover withdrawn land: only land leased under the Land Act is outside Crown range. Terms on the use of the withdrawn land decide whether grazing is compatible.

terms.where: The withdrawal's record on the Crown lands file
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship (Crown land administration)
terms.channel: FrontCounter BC, quoting the Crown lands file number
terms.ask: The withdrawal's purpose, its effective date and any terms and conditions imposed on the use of the land

binds.note: The minister designates Crown land for a particular use, and the land is then withdrawn from disposition under the Land Act for any purpose the minister finds incompatible with it. A Forest Act agreement to harvest Crown timber is not a Land Act disposition. Decision-makers consider the designation; it does not itself regulate forest work unless its terms do. This is a reading of the Act's text; no court decision on the point was found.

harvest.note: The designation withdraws land from Land Act disposition for incompatible purposes, which on this reading does not bar a Forest Act harvest. The minister may impose terms and conditions on the use of the designated land, and only the designation's notice and land use report say whether they reach timber harvesting. This is a reading of the Act's text; no court decision on the point was found.

replant.note: The designation's terms on the use of the land decide whether site preparation and planting fit its purpose. The free-growing duty is FRPA's, and the designation does not lift it.

roads.note: A forest service road is kept out of the Crown land registry like a timber agreement. The designation's terms on the use of the land decide whether a road fits its purpose.

grazing.note: A designation is not a lease, so its land can be Crown range under a Range Act agreement. The designation's purpose and terms decide how grazing fits; a designation for agriculture and grazing is common on range.

terms.where: The signed notice of establishment and any land use report
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship (Crown land administration)
terms.channel: FrontCounter BC, quoting the Crown lands file number
terms.ask: The notice of establishment of the designated use area, its land use report and any terms and conditions imposed on the use of the land, with its effective date and whether it has been reviewed or continued

binds.note: An executed lease is an interest in Crown land, binding on the government once executed, held on the terms the minister imposed. The Act does not make a lease a bar to a Forest Act harvest; the lessee's rights are in its terms, which decision-makers consider.

harvest.note: Leased land is still Crown land, so its timber is Crown timber. What the lease grants the lessee, and what forest work on it needs, are in its terms. For a grazing lease the 2004 grazing policy reviews a timber harvest with the lessee (policy, not law).

replant.note: The lease's terms decide whether planting fits its purpose. The free-growing duty is FRPA's.

roads.note: The lease's terms decide whether a road may cross it.

grazing.note: The Range Act's Crown range excludes Crown land leased under the Land Act, so no Range Act agreement covers it and grazing there is only under the lease's own terms. FPPR s. 44(3)(d)'s exemption, which needs a Range Act agreement, cannot rest on a lease.

terms.where: The executed lease and its legal description
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship (Crown land administration)
terms.channel: FrontCounter BC, quoting the Crown lands file and document numbers
terms.ask: The lease's terms on the use of the land, any clause on timber, access or consent, and its term and expiry

binds.note: An executed licence is an interest in Crown land held on the terms the minister imposed. The Act does not make it a bar to a Forest Act harvest; the licensee's rights are in its terms, which decision-makers consider.

harvest.note: The licence's terms decide what the licensee holds and what forest work on its area needs. The land stays Crown land, so its timber is Crown timber.

replant.note: The licence's terms decide whether planting fits its purpose. The free-growing duty is FRPA's.

roads.note: The licence's terms decide whether a road may cross it.

grazing.note: A licence is not a lease, so its land can still be Crown range under a Range Act agreement. The licence's terms decide whether grazing fits.

terms.where: The executed licence of occupation
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship (Crown land administration)
terms.channel: FrontCounter BC, quoting the Crown lands file and document numbers

binds.note: A right of way is a statutory right of way over Crown land, held on the terms the minister imposed. The Act does not make it a bar to a Forest Act harvest; the holder's rights are in its terms, which decision-makers consider.

harvest.note: The right of way's terms decide what clearing and work on the corridor needs, and what its holder may require. The land stays Crown land, so its timber is Crown timber.

replant.note: The right of way's terms decide whether trees may be re-established on the corridor. The free-growing duty is FRPA's.

roads.note: The right of way's terms decide whether, and how, a road may cross the corridor.

grazing.note: A right of way is not a lease, so its land can still be Crown range under a Range Act agreement. Its terms decide whether grazing fits.

terms.where: The executed right of way
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship (Crown land administration)
terms.channel: FrontCounter BC, quoting the Crown lands file and document numbers
terms.ask: The right of way's purpose, width and terms on clearing, crossings and access

instruments.label: Tantalis notation of interest
instruments.note: A notation of interest is a record in the Crown land registry, not a disposition: it marks a feature or concern (a trapline cabin, a First Nation cultural feature, a salt lick) so its holder is referred to on Land Act applications.

binds.note: The policy makes a notation of interest "not an authorization under the Land Act, but rather a notation to identify a feature or concern", used to refer Land Act applications to the agency holding it; it "does not preclude the acceptance and decision of Crown land applications". It is not one of the Act's dispositions.

harvest.note: The notation authorizes and forbids nothing itself, and the policy speaks only of Land Act applications. What it marks, and whether that feature (a cabin, a cultural feature, a lick) needs care in harvesting, is in its notice of establishment.

replant.note: The notation sets nothing on planting; what it marks is in its notice of establishment.

roads.note: The notation sets nothing on roads; what it marks, and whether a road would touch it, is in its notice of establishment.

grazing.note: The notation sets nothing on grazing; what it marks is in its notice of establishment. The land stays Crown range unless leased under the Land Act.

terms.where: The notice establishing the notation (the policy's Appendix 4 template), on the Crown lands file
terms.holder: The provincial or federal agency that asked for the notation, through the Crown land registry
terms.channel: FrontCounter BC, quoting the Crown lands file number
terms.ask: The notice establishing the notation of interest: the interest or feature it marks, the agency holding it, its term and its review date

instruments.label: Land Act application (not yet a disposition)
instruments.note: A Tantalis record at stage APPLICATION: someone has applied for a lease, licence, right of way, sale or other disposition of this Crown land. A §15–17 designation or a notation at application stage is listed under its own row.

binds.note: Filing an application gives no right in or priority to the land, and a disposition binds the government only once executed; the government need not consider or grant it. It signals that a disposition may be decided here, and an accepted application is published.

harvest.note: An application creates no right in the land and binds the government to nothing until a disposition is executed. If a disposition is issued, its terms decide what forest work on it needs, and the lease, licence or right of way row then applies.

replant.note: An application creates no right in the land until a disposition is executed.

roads.note: An application creates no right in the land until a disposition is executed.

grazing.note: An application creates no right in the land; only land leased under the Land Act leaves Crown range, and an application is not a lease.

terms.where: The application as the province publishes it once accepted (Land Act s. 32(2)), on the Crown lands file
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship (Crown land administration)
terms.channel: The province's published applications, or FrontCounter BC quoting the Crown lands file number
terms.ask: The application: what is applied for, its purpose and term, and where the decision stands

binds.note: The Act restricts the use of agricultural land, Crown land included (in relation to Crown land, the owner is the government): non-farm use, and soil removal or fill placement, need a permission, a notice or a use the regulation permits.

harvest.note: Producing and harvesting timber, including silviculture and forest protection, is a designated farm use that a local government or first nation law may not prohibit; the Act's restriction is on non-farm use. Other enactments still apply.

replant.note: Silviculture is part of the designated farm use of producing and harvesting timber.

roads.note: Removing soil from or placing fill on agricultural land needs the Commission's permission, an approved notice, or a use the regulation permits. The regulation's permitted soil and fill uses list no new forest road, and its permitted road works are within dedicated rights of way and forest service roads. Whether a new block road is part of the farm use of producing timber is not stated.

grazing.note: Farming animals is a farm use.

terms.where: The Act, the regulation, and any Commission decision on the land
terms.holder: Agricultural Land Commission
terms.channel: Agricultural Land Commission
terms.ask: Any Commission decision, condition or soil and fill notice on the land

instruments.label: Wildlife habitat area, harvest zone not coded

binds.note: Whoever carries out primary forest activities on the area must comply with each general wildlife measure that applies, and a range agreement holder's range practices must be consistent with them. A forest stewardship plan is amended when a wildlife habitat area objective affects one of its units.

harvest.note: The layer gives this area no timber harvest code. Only the order's general wildlife measures say what harvest they allow, and they must be complied with.

replant.note: Silviculture is a primary forest activity bound by the measures; only the order's measures say what they require of it.

roads.note: Road construction is a primary forest activity bound by the measures; only the order's measures say what they require of it.

grazing.note: Range practices must be consistent with the measures; only the order's measures say what they require of grazing.

terms.where: The order establishing the habitat area and its general wildlife measures, given notice in the Gazette
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship
terms.channel: The ministry's approved wildlife habitat area orders (https://www.env.gov.bc.ca/wld/frpa/iwms/wha.html), by the WHA tag
terms.ask: The order and its general wildlife measures for the area

binds.note: The agreement grants grazing or hay rights over Crown range. FRPA's range developments and natural range barriers provisions, and the range regulation's livestock removal rule, apply to the forest work and the grazing on it directly.

harvest.note: A forest practice that removes or renders ineffective a natural range barrier must carry out the operational plan's or the minister's mitigation, and carrying out, modifying, removing or damaging a range development on Crown range needs the minister's written authorization.

replant.note: Grazing shares the ground with the new stand: an agreement holder who knows grazing will significantly interfere with establishing a free-growing stand must remove the livestock and keep them out. The free-growing duty is lifted only where harvest is restricted to land used, or to be used, exclusively for grazing or hay under a Range Act agreement.

roads.note: A road that cuts, removes or damages a range development (a fence, gate, cattleguard or water development) needs the minister's written authorization, and one that removes a natural range barrier needs its mitigation.

grazing.note: The agreement grants the grazing or hay rights, and its holder needs an approved range use plan or range stewardship plan before grazing.

terms.where: The agreement, and its range use plan or range stewardship plan with the schedule of grazing, pastures and range developments
terms.holder: The natural resource district's range staff
terms.channel: The natural resource district, quoting the RAN file
terms.ask: The range use plan or range stewardship plan for the block's pasture, its grazing schedule, and the range developments and natural range barriers it records near the block

binds.note: A natural resource in a park must not be removed, destroyed, disturbed or exploited except as a park use permit authorizes (in a recreation area, as the minister approves), and an interest in a Class A or C park's land only by park use permit.

harvest.note: Timber is a natural resource of the park: removing it needs a park use permit (Class A, B or C park) or the minister's approval (recreation area). Timber cut in a park is disposed of under the Forest Act.

replant.note: Site preparation and planting disturb the park's natural resources and need the same permit or approval.

roads.note: A road takes an interest in, and disturbs, the park's land: a park use permit, or the minister's approval in a recreation area.

grazing.note: Grazing uses the park's vegetation, which needs a permit or approval. In a Schedule D park a range tenure in effect when the park was established continues under the Range Act, capped at the animal unit months then authorized.

terms.where: The Park Act, the park's establishing instrument and its management plan
terms.holder: BC Parks
terms.channel: BC Parks
terms.ask: The park's boundary at the block and any park use permit or approval in force there

binds.note: An ecological reserve is withdrawn and reserved from any further disposition under any Act, the Forest Act and the Range Act among them; use and occupation are only by permit for research or education.

harvest.note: No Forest Act disposition can be granted in it.

replant.note: Use and occupation are only by permit for ecological research or education.

roads.note: No Forest Act or Land Act disposition can be granted in it.

grazing.note: No Range Act disposition can be granted in it.

terms.where: The Ecological Reserve Act and the reserve's establishing instrument
terms.holder: BC Parks
terms.channel: BC Parks
terms.ask: The reserve's boundary at the block

binds.note: A protected area is established by its own instrument, which the area's record names: an Environment and Land Use Act order, which ministers must exercise their other powers in accordance with, or a Park Act designation.

harvest.note: The area's establishing order decides.

replant.note: The area's establishing order decides.

roads.note: The area's establishing order decides.

grazing.note: The area's establishing order decides.

terms.where: The order or designation that established the protected area
terms.holder: BC Parks
terms.channel: BC Parks, quoting the area's name
terms.ask: The instrument that established the protected area, and what it allows inside it

binds.note: The parcel is not Crown land, so its timber is not Crown timber unless it is reserved to the government. The owner's title, not a Crown disposition, decides what happens on it.

harvest.note: A Crown timber disposition does not reach private land, except timber reserved to the government, which is Crown timber. Harvesting the owner's timber is the owner's to allow. Private managed forest land is a different regime and is not assessed here.

replant.note: FRPA's free-growing duty attaches to a harvest under a forest stewardship, forest operations or woodlot licence plan; on private land outside one the owner decides. Private managed forest land is not assessed here.

roads.note: A road on the parcel needs the owner's agreement: it is not Crown land.

grazing.note: Crown range is Crown land; a Range Act agreement does not reach private land.

terms.where: The title, and any reservation of timber to the government
terms.holder: The natural resource district (no owner is read or contacted from this screen)
terms.channel: The natural resource district, quoting the PID
terms.ask: Whether the parcel's timber is reserved to the government, and whether the block should be redrawn off the parcel

binds.note: FPPR's water rules apply to primary forest activities in a community watershed directly, and the objective for water in it reaches the forest stewardship plan. Range practices are bound by the range regulation's water rules.

harvest.note: A primary forest activity must not deposit material harmful to human health in water diverted by a licensed waterworks or damage the works, and no harvest is within 100 m upslope of an intake unless it will not increase sediment delivery to it.

replant.note: Silviculture is a primary forest activity bound by the same water rules, fertilizer near a waterworks or a perennial stream is limited, and livestock used for site preparation stay out of riparian management areas in the watershed.

roads.note: No road within 100 m upslope of an intake unless it will not increase sediment delivery, roads kept back from identified springs, and affected water licensees notified 48 hours before construction or deactivation.

grazing.note: Range practices must not harm the water or the waterworks, must be consistent with any water quality objective, and dead livestock are kept 100 m from streams in the watershed.

terms.where: The regulations, and any water quality objective established for the watershed
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship
terms.channel: The natural resource district
terms.ask: Any water quality objective for the watershed, and the licensed waterworks intakes and springs near the block

instruments.label: Mineral or placer tenure
instruments.note: Mineral and placer claims and leases under the Mineral Tenure Act. Coal tenures, under the Coal Act, are not read.

binds.note: A recorded holder may use, enter and occupy the claim's surface for exploring for and producing minerals, once any Mines Act permit is issued. The holder does not own the timber: on request it is issued a free use permit or an occupant licence to cut under the Forest Act. A later disposition of surface rights does not diminish the holder's rights except as an order or agreement determines.

harvest.note: The Act gives the holder surface rights for mining, not the timber, which stays Crown timber disposed of under the Forest Act. Whether a timber harvest is a disposition of surface rights that may not diminish the holder's rights is not stated; the chief gold commissioner's or minister's order, or an agreement, decides. This is a reading of the Act's text; no court decision on the point was read.

replant.note: The holder may occupy the surface for mining; whether planting conflicts with its exploration or a Mines Act permit is in the title's record and any permit.

roads.note: The holder may occupy the surface for mining and its own access. Whether a road for a block over the claim interferes with the holder's rights is in the title's record and any Mines Act permit.

grazing.note: Claim land stays Crown range; whether grazing conflicts with the holder's use of the surface is in the title's record and any permit.

terms.where: The title's record in the mineral titles registry, and any Mines Act permit or notice of work on it
terms.holder: The chief gold commissioner (Mineral Titles)
terms.channel: Mineral Titles, quoting the tenure number
terms.ask: The title's status and good-to date, any order under Mineral Tenure Act s. 13 or 17 on it, and any Mines Act permit or notice of work for the area

instruments.label: Water licence point of diversion
instruments.note: Current licences only; a point of diversion can carry several licences, each listed. Counted inside the footprint and within the layer's stated margin of it.

binds.note: The licence entitles its holder to divert and use water and to build and operate the works. A primary forest activity must not damage a licensed waterworks or put material harmful to human health in water diverted for human consumption; in a community watershed harvesting and roads keep 100 m upslope of such an intake unless sediment delivery will not increase. Anyone proposing to interfere with works must give the holder 180 days' written notice.

harvest.note: Harvesting must not damage the works or put material harmful to human health in water diverted for human consumption, and in a community watershed it keeps 100 m upslope of such an intake unless it will not increase sediment delivery to it.

replant.note: Silviculture is a primary forest activity bound by the same water rules; in a community watershed fertilizer is limited within 100 m upslope of a licensed waterworks.

roads.note: Roads must not damage the works; in a community watershed they keep 100 m upslope of an intake for human consumption unless sediment delivery will not increase, and affected water licensees are notified 48 hours before construction. Altering or interfering with works needs the holder's 180 days' notice.

grazing.note: Range practices must not put material harmful to human health in water diverted for human consumption, and where they could materially harm a licensed waterworks must not damage it or alter the vegetation, soil or terrain around it.

terms.where: The water licence, by its licence and point of diversion numbers
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship (water authorizations)
terms.channel: FrontCounter BC, quoting the licence and point of diversion numbers
terms.ask: The licence's purpose, works and intake location, whether its water is diverted for human consumption, and any conditions on the land round the works

instruments.label: Woodlot licence
instruments.note: Active records only, told apart by the forest file's letter (W), as the old forest land base reads them. A woodlot licence's Schedule B is Crown land and Schedule A private land owned or leased by the holder, or reserve land.

binds.note: An area-based licence: the Forest Act requires it to give its holder the exclusive right to harvest timber on its Crown land for its term. That right gives way to a BC Timber Sales licence only where the holder released harvesting rights to the government under a BCTS disposition agreement.

harvest.note: Only the holder may harvest the Crown timber in it, and a timber sale over it needs the holder's rights released under a BCTS disposition agreement. Schedule A land is the holder's own or a reserve, outside Crown timber altogether.

replant.note: A harvest by the holder carries the holder's own reforestation obligation; what the licence and its plan require beyond that is in the licence document.

roads.note: The licence document and its plan decide road building in the area, and whether a road for a block outside it may cross.

grazing.note: The licence grants timber rights; its Crown land stays Crown range. Whether the licence's terms restrict grazing is in the licence document.

terms.where: The licence document and its management plan
terms.holder: Ministry of Forests, the natural resource district (tenures)
terms.channel: The natural resource district, quoting the forest file id
terms.ask: The licence's area (Schedules A and B), term and conditions, and its current management plan; whether any of its harvesting rights are released to BC Timber Sales

instruments.label: Community forest agreement
instruments.note: Active records only, told apart by the forest file's letter (K), as the old forest land base reads them. Its area is Crown land and any private or reserve land the minister includes.

binds.note: An area-based licence: the Forest Act requires it to give its holder the exclusive right to harvest timber on its Crown land for its term. That right gives way to a BC Timber Sales licence only where the holder released harvesting rights to the government under a BCTS disposition agreement.

harvest.note: Only the holder may harvest the Crown timber in it, and a timber sale over it needs the holder's rights released under a BCTS disposition agreement. Its forest stewardship plan must be consistent with the timber harvesting rights the agreement grants.

replant.note: A harvest by the holder carries the holder's own reforestation obligation; what the licence and its plan require beyond that is in the licence document.

roads.note: The licence document and its plan decide road building in the area, and whether a road for a block outside it may cross.

grazing.note: The licence grants timber rights; its Crown land stays Crown range. Whether the licence's terms restrict grazing is in the licence document.

terms.where: The licence document and its management plan
terms.holder: Ministry of Forests, the natural resource district (tenures)
terms.channel: The natural resource district, quoting the forest file id
terms.ask: The licence's area (Schedules A and B), term and conditions, and its current management plan; whether any of its harvesting rights are released to BC Timber Sales

instruments.label: First Nations woodland licence
instruments.note: Active records only, told apart by the forest file's letter (N), as the old forest land base reads them. Its area is Crown land and any private or reserve land the minister includes.

binds.note: An area-based licence: the Forest Act requires it to give its holder the exclusive right to harvest timber on its Crown land for its term. That right gives way to a BC Timber Sales licence only where the holder released harvesting rights to the government under a BCTS disposition agreement.

harvest.note: Only the holder may harvest the Crown timber in it, and a timber sale over it needs the holder's rights released under a BCTS disposition agreement. The licence implements an agreement between the First Nation and the government.

replant.note: A harvest by the holder carries the holder's own reforestation obligation; what the licence and its plan require beyond that is in the licence document.

roads.note: The licence document and its plan decide road building in the area, and whether a road for a block outside it may cross.

grazing.note: The licence grants timber rights; its Crown land stays Crown range. Whether the licence's terms restrict grazing is in the licence document.

instruments.note: The licences' current boundaries, asked by each footprint part's hull because each TFL is one very detailed polygon, as the old forest land base reads them. A TFL area is Crown land, and any private land or timber licence land the minister includes.

binds.note: An area-based licence: the Forest Act requires it to give its holder the exclusive right to harvest timber on its Crown land for its term. That right gives way to a BC Timber Sales licence only where the holder released harvesting rights to the government under a BCTS disposition agreement.

The licence also requires timber, in an amount the minister directs, to be made available to others for BC Timber Sales, pulpwood agreements and woodlot licences.

replant.note: A harvest by the holder carries the holder's own reforestation obligation; what the licence and its plan require beyond that is in the licence document.

roads.note: The licence document and its plan decide road building in the area, and whether a road for a block outside it may cross.

grazing.note: The licence grants timber rights; its Crown land stays Crown range. Whether the licence's terms restrict grazing is in the licence document.

instruments.label: Recreation site, interpretive forest or trail-based recreation area
instruments.note: Active records. `PROJECT_ESTABLISHED_DATE` is the date the feature was legally established; some records leave it blank. Recreation reserves in the same layer are not established under s. 56 and are not read.

binds.note: Established by the minister's order, which may set an objective for it. A recreation site, trail or interpretive forest is a resource feature: an authorized person carrying out a primary forest activity must not damage it or render it ineffective. The minister may also order a non-recreational use of it restricted or prohibited, with notice posted on the ground.

harvest.note: Harvesting must not damage the site or render it ineffective in any case. The establishing order's objective, and any order restricting or prohibiting non-recreational use, decide what more applies.

replant.note: Silviculture is a primary forest activity that must not damage the site; the establishing order's objective, and any restricting order, decide more.

roads.note: Road work must not damage the site; the establishing order's objective, and any restricting order, decide more. Building a trail or recreation facility needs the minister's written authorization.

grazing.note: The minister may restrict or prohibit a non-recreational use of the site by order to protect a recreation or range resource; only such an order says whether grazing is restricted.

terms.where: The order establishing the site and any objective for it, and any order under FRPA s. 58
terms.holder: Recreation Sites and Trails BC (Ministry of Forests)
terms.channel: The district recreation officer, quoting the recreation file
terms.ask: The order establishing the site, any objective established for it, and any order restricting or prohibiting non-recreational use

instruments.label: Recreation trail
instruments.note: Active, established trails, measured by their length inside the footprint and within the layer's stated margin of it. Trail reserves are not established under s. 56 and are not read.

binds.note: Established by the minister's order, which may set an objective for it. A recreation site, trail or interpretive forest is a resource feature: an authorized person carrying out a primary forest activity must not damage it or render it ineffective. The minister may also order a non-recreational use of it restricted or prohibited, with notice posted on the ground.

harvest.note: Harvesting must not damage the trail or render it ineffective in any case. The establishing order's objective, and any order restricting or prohibiting non-recreational use, decide what more applies.

replant.note: Silviculture is a primary forest activity that must not damage the site; the establishing order's objective, and any restricting order, decide more.

roads.note: Road work must not damage the site; the establishing order's objective, and any restricting order, decide more. Building a trail or recreation facility needs the minister's written authorization.

grazing.note: The minister may restrict or prohibit a non-recreational use of the trail by order to protect a recreation or range resource; only such an order says whether grazing is restricted.

terms.where: The order establishing the trail and any objective for it, and any order under FRPA s. 58
terms.holder: Recreation Sites and Trails BC (Ministry of Forests)
terms.channel: The district recreation officer, quoting the recreation file
terms.ask: The order establishing the trail, any objective established for it, and any order restricting or prohibiting non-recreational use

instruments.label: Established visual quality objective
instruments.note: The inventory's established VQO (P preservation, R retention, PR partial retention, M modification, MM maximum modification). An objective established for a scenic area under the GAR, continued from the Code (FRPA s. 181), or a visual quality class a district manager's letter set before 24 October 2002 (GAR s. 17); the inventory does not say which.

binds.note: A visual quality objective is an objective established under the Act for a scenic area; a forest stewardship plan must specify results or strategies for it, and its holder must achieve and carry them out. Each category is an extent of alteration from the size, shape and location of cutblocks and roads, assessed from a significant public viewpoint.

harvest.note: Cutblocks may be made, within the category's extent of visible alteration from significant public viewpoints, as the FSP's result or strategy for the objective says.

replant.note: The categories are judged on the size, shape and location of cutblocks and roads; they set nothing on planting. How fast a stand greens up bears on how long an alteration stays visible, which the FSP's strategy may address.

roads.note: Roads count in the alteration the category allows.

grazing.note: The categories are judged on cutblocks and roads; nothing in them reaches grazing. A range use plan must be consistent with objectives established under the Act.

terms.where: The inventory's established objective and the regulation's categories; the establishing order or letter where one is needed
terms.holder: Ministry of Forests, the natural resource district
terms.channel: The natural resource district
terms.ask: The order or letter that established the objective for the scenic area, and the significant public viewpoints it is assessed from

instruments.label: Scenic area without an established objective
instruments.note: Inventory polygons made known as a scenic area with no established VQO in the inventory (any code other than P, R, PR, M or MM prints as DataBC gives it).

binds.note: For a scenic area established on or before 24 October 2002 with no visual quality objective, the objective set by government is a pair of categories by its visual sensitivity class (class 1 preservation or retention, 2 retention or partial retention, 3 and 4 partial retention or modification, 5 modification or maximum modification). A forest stewardship plan must specify results or strategies for it.

harvest.note: Where the scenic area predates 24 October 2002, harvesting is held to the categories for its visual sensitivity class, which the inventory gives. A scenic area established later under the GAR with no objective has none from s. 9.2. When it was made known is in the establishing order or letter, not the layer.

replant.note: The categories are judged on cutblocks and roads; they set nothing on planting.

roads.note: Roads count in the alteration, where s. 9.2's objective applies; whether it does turns on when the scenic area was made known.

grazing.note: The categories are judged on cutblocks and roads; nothing in them reaches grazing.

terms.where: The regulation, and the inventory's visual sensitivity class; the order or letter that made the scenic area known
terms.holder: Ministry of Forests, the natural resource district
terms.channel: The natural resource district
terms.ask: When and how the scenic area was made known, and whether a visual quality objective has since been established for it

instruments.label: Federal critical habitat (Species at Risk Act)
instruments.note: Critical habitat identified in a federal recovery strategy or action plan, final or proposed, as ECCC posts it; secure polygons are not public. One habitat can span hundreds of thousands of hectares (a caribou range's matrix), so the overlap is the share of the block, not of the habitat.

binds.note: On land in a province that is not federal land, the prohibition on destroying any part of a listed endangered or threatened species' critical habitat applies only to the portions a Governor in Council order specifies, on the federal minister's recommendation; an emergency order can also prohibit activities that may adversely affect the species and its habitat. On federal land the prohibition applies through the minister's order or the protected-area description. Without such an order the identification alone regulates nothing on provincial Crown land; provincial measures (a winter range, a habitat area, a conservation agreement) are separate.

harvest.note: Destroying any part of the critical habitat is prohibited on provincial Crown land only where an order under s. 61(2), or an emergency order under s. 80, specifies that portion. None was looked for in this read; the Species at Risk Public Registry and the Canada Gazette list them. On federal land (the layer's land tenure) the s. 58 order decides.

replant.note: Whether planting could destroy part of the habitat, and whether any order reaches it, is in the order and the recovery strategy that identified the habitat.

roads.note: A road can destroy part of the habitat; the prohibition reaches it only where an order specifies the portion.

grazing.note: The prohibition reaches grazing only where an order specifies the portion and the grazing destroys part of the habitat.

terms.where: The recovery strategy or action plan that identified the habitat, and any order under SARA s. 58, 61 or 80, on the Species at Risk Public Registry
terms.holder: Environment and Climate Change Canada
terms.channel: The Species at Risk Public Registry; ECCC's Canadian Wildlife Service, Pacific region
terms.ask: Whether any order under SARA s. 58(4), 61(2) or 80 applies to this portion of the critical habitat, and which provincial measures the federal minister relies on to protect it

instruments.label: Candidate old forest area (Prince George TSA, 2022 letter of expectations)
instruments.note: Non-legal OGMA records numbered PRG_COFA: the COFAs the letter's Appendix 5 says are in this layer. Not legally designated: a candidate the reviewer confirms against the letter and the district.

binds.note: A district manager's expectation, not an enactment: the COFAs "are not legally designated or considered an amendment to the Order", and the 2004 order's Objectives A and B stay the legal test. The Prince George district manager presents the letter as information "I consider to be of weight", and expects the COFAs to be respected as no harvest areas.

harvest.note: Expected to be left unharvested and avoided in harvest planning; an incursion is considered only by the district manager's variance, where the impact is unavoidable and an alternative area of equal or greater value is identified, and "All incursions require approval", forecast in the annual summary of requested variances. An expectation, not a legal requirement.

replant.note: The letter sets nothing on planting or reforestation; COFAs lost to wildfire or forest health agents are not replaced.

roads.note: A road into a COFA is an incursion like a block: the variance process and the annual summary, which includes planned road locations, apply.

grazing.note: The letter is about harvest planning and old forest retention; it sets nothing on grazing.

terms.where: The district managers' letter of expectations, 21 December 2022; its Appendix 5 describes the layer
terms.holder: Prince George Natural Resource District
terms.channel: The district manager, through the annual summary of requested variances
terms.ask: Whether the incursion would be considered for a variance, the replacement area expected, and whether the COFA is still current

instruments.label: 2009 non-legal OGMA counted with the COFAs (Prince George TSA, mBEC A22 or A23)
instruments.note: Non-legal OGMA records numbered PRG_DPG in mBEC A22 or A23, which Appendix 5 says are viewed with the COFAs; the PRG_DPG records in A04, which it excepts, are not asked for, nor two slivers with no reason given.

binds.note: Appendix 5: the legacy (2009) non-legal OGMAs in mBECs A22 and A23 "contribute towards the spatialization of old growth under the Order", so the COFAs and these are read together to see all the spatialized old growth. Not legally designated; the letter's no-harvest expectation names the COFAs.

harvest.note: Whether the district manager's no-harvest expectation and variance process reach these as they reach the COFAs is not stated; the district decides. They count toward the order's targets.

replant.note: The letter sets nothing on planting or reforestation.

roads.note: As for harvest: the district decides whether a road into one is treated as a COFA incursion.

grazing.note: The letter sets nothing on grazing.

terms.where: The district managers' letter of expectations, Appendix 5; the district's 2009 non-legal OGMA direction
terms.holder: Prince George Natural Resource District
terms.channel: The natural resource district
terms.ask: Whether the no-harvest expectation and the COFA variance process apply to this 2009 non-legal OGMA

instruments.label: Special purpose area (Forest Act Part 15)
instruments.note: Designated by regulation for an access, non-timber production, First Nation, BC Timber Sales or community forest purpose, for at most 3 years unless extended. The BC Data Catalogue says the layer holds no record because no special purpose area is in effect (checked 27 November 2026), so a read finds none; a designation can be made retroactive to 15 July 2023 (s. 225(2)).

binds.note: Part 15 binds the officials who issue Forest Act licences, permits and road permits, and lets the minister amend, suspend or cancel rights already granted in the area.

harvest.note: No cutting permit, timber sale licence, forestry licence to cut or free use permit may be issued with rights in the area, except a licence to cut for fire, forest health or public safety, its cutting permit, or a free use permit for science, a traditional and cultural activity or a treaty first nation (s. 209(2)), or a licence entered into for the designation's own purposes (s. 223); rights already granted may be amended, suspended or cancelled.

replant.note: Part 15 restricts licences, roads and timber production improvements, not planting; whether reforestation under an existing obligation fits the area's purpose is not stated. The designating regulation names the purpose.

roads.note: After designation no new road may be authorized under a road permit or special use permit unless an official is satisfied of a s. 215(2) ground; a road under an earlier permit must not be built without the minister's order, and existing roads may be ordered deactivated or their permits amended, suspended or cancelled.

grazing.note: Part 15 names no Range Act agreement; it protects livestock fencing only as an ancillary road structure. The designating regulation's purpose, and the enactment that purpose serves, decide.

terms.where: The regulation designating the area (its B.C. Reg. number), which states the purpose and cancellation date
terms.holder: Ministry of Forests
terms.channel: BC Laws, by the regulation number; the natural resource district
terms.ask: The designating regulation, any extension, and any order made under Part 15 for licences, permits or roads in the area

instruments.label: Pine-leading stand of 5 ha or more in a listed area (candidate targeted pine leading stand)
instruments.note: VRI rank 1 polygons whose leading species is lodgepole pine (PL, PLI, PLC) and whose polygon is 5 ha or more, read only in the listed TSAs and TFLs. The inventory does not map secondary structure, so whether the stand has an adequate stocking density of it, and so is a targeted stand, is the reviewer's.

binds.note: A holder of a cutting permit, a forestry licence to cut without cutting permits or a timber sale licence must not harvest in a targeted pine leading stand unless one of s. 43.1(1)'s cases or s. 43.1(2)'s exceptions applies; the section does not apply to the holders and areas s. 43.1(4) lists.

harvest.note: Harvest only to fell a safety hazard, to build a road with no other practicable location, or retaining an adequate stocking density of suitable secondary structure, unless the stand is at significant blowdown risk, at least 30% of its pine holds live beetles, harvest protects a community from wildfire, or it collects seed in an opening of 1 ha or less.

replant.note: Where harvest leaves an obligation to establish a free growing stand, each retained tree of suitable secondary structure counts as a preferred species where it was retained.

roads.note: Harvest to build a road through the stand is allowed only where there is no other practicable location; a road permit is outside the section.

grazing.note: The section governs timber harvesting by the listed holders; it sets nothing on grazing.

terms.where: The regulation; the government-endorsed forest cover map, a cruise of the stand, and any chief forester order under FPPR s. 43.2
terms.holder: Ministry of Forests
terms.channel: The natural resource district
terms.ask: Any chief forester order under FPPR s. 43.2 for the area, and the cruise or survey of secondary structure in the stand

instruments.label: Fisheries sensitive watershed
instruments.note: Watersheds identified by order under the Government Actions Regulation; the 17 identified only under the Oil and Gas Activities Act are left out.

binds.note: The order may establish a fisheries sensitive watershed objective; a forest stewardship plan must identify the watershed for its forest development unit, specify results or strategies for an objective established under FRPA, and be amended when one is set.

cites.provision: s. 1 "fisheries sensitive watershed objective", s. 14(3)(c), s. 28.1(1)(e)

harvest.note: The order's objective for the watershed, and the forest stewardship plan's results or strategies for it, decide what harvest it allows (often by equivalent clearcut area).

replant.note: The order's objective decides; hydrological recovery may depend on regeneration.

roads.note: The order's objective decides; stream channel integrity and the timing of flow are what it protects.

grazing.note: A range use plan must be consistent with an objective established under FRPA; the order decides what it sets.

terms.where: The order identifying the watershed and any objective for it, given notice
terms.holder: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship
terms.channel: The ministry's approved fisheries sensitive watershed orders (https://www.env.gov.bc.ca/wld/frpa/fsw/approved.html), by the FSW tag
terms.ask: The order and its objective for the unit, and the forest stewardship plan's results or strategies for it

instruments.label: Forest development unit of an approved forest stewardship plan (candidate)
instruments.note: The units of each plan's current approved amendment. A candidate: the layer does not say whether the plan is held by the holder applying for the block (no holder's or client's name or number is read), and an approved plan whose term has ended still shows, with its end date. The reviewer confirms both from the plan.

binds.note: An approved forest stewardship plan binds its holders: they must achieve its intended results, carry out its strategies and comply with the provisions that relate to them, and the duty continues after the plan expires or a holder is removed, as the plan then read, unless another plan replaces the provision. It binds no one else.

harvest.note: Outside a forest landscape area, a unit of its holder's approved plan containing the land is what lets the holder apply for a cutting permit and harvest there (FRPA s. 3(1), (2)). What harvest the plan allows is in its intended results and strategies, as it read when the permit was issued; the layer carries neither them nor whether the applicant holds the plan. The FSP decides.

replant.note: The plan's stocking standards, and the situations that decide which applies, set its holders' regeneration and free growing obligations. The FSP decides.

roads.note: A unit containing the land is what lets the holder apply for a road permit and build a road there (FRPA s. 3(1)(b), (d), (2)(b), (c)); the plan's results and strategies, for soils and permanent access among them, decide what more applies. The FSP decides.

grazing.note: The plan binds its holders, who carry out forest practices; grazing on Crown range is the Range Act agreement's. The measures the plan must specify for natural range barriers mitigate a forest practice that removes one, not grazing.

terms.where: The forest stewardship plan as approved and amended: its map of forest development units (FRPA s. 5(1)(a)), its intended results and strategies, its stocking standards and its identified areas, by FSP id
terms.holder: The plan's holder; the natural resource district
terms.channel: The holder, who must make the plan publicly available (FRPA s. 20.25(2)); a BC Timber Sales plan is on a ministry website (s. 20.25(3)). The FSP Tracking System holds the plan by FSP id but needs a government sign-in, so no public link is given
terms.ask: The plan and amendment in effect for the block, its term and any extension (FRPA s. 6(2)), the agreements and holders it applies to, and its results, strategies and stocking standards for the forest development unit

instruments.label: Forest development unit in a forest stewardship plan or amendment submitted, not yet approved
instruments.note: Units of a plan or amendment awaiting the minister's decision. Drafts are not read; earlier amendments' units (status PREVIOUS) are not read either.

binds.note: A plan or amendment awaiting decision authorizes nothing and binds no one: FRPA s. 3 asks for an approved plan, one the minister has approved, which the minister does on the tests of s. 16(1).

harvest.note: Until approved, the unit does not let a holder apply for a cutting permit or harvest on its land; once approved, the approved unit's row applies.

replant.note: A submitted plan's stocking standards bind no one until it is approved.

roads.note: Until approved, the unit does not let a holder apply for a road permit or build a road on its land.

grazing.note: Neither a submitted nor an approved plan regulates grazing; it binds its holders' forest practices.

terms.where: The plan or amendment as submitted, made publicly available for review and comment before it was submitted (FPPR ss. 20, 21)
terms.holder: The plan's proponent; the natural resource district
terms.channel: The proponent's review notice (FPPR s. 20(1)), or the district, by FSP id
terms.ask: Whether the submitted plan or amendment adds the block's area to a forest development unit, and when the minister's decision is expected

instruments.label: Area of a forest development plan's cutblock or road carried into a forest stewardship plan (FRPA s. 196)
instruments.note: Identified areas a plan specifies under FPPR s. 14(1)(c): a cutblock or road a forest development plan included, for which the plan's parts are considered approved. These are not the areas FPPR s. 14(2) and (3) require a plan to identify (winter ranges, watersheds and the rest), which the layer does not hold.

binds.note: The plan's parts that pertain to the area are considered to have the minister's approval, and its holders carry them out like any other part. Unless the plan says otherwise, the Code and its regulations continue for a cutblock or road right of way under a permit in effect when the plan was approved.

harvest.note: Harvest of the cutblock rests on the forest development plan that included it with its assessments completed, and on the plan's parts for it, considered approved unless an enactment, objective, community watershed or catastrophic damage changed in the period of s. 196(3) and the minister considers the unit inconsistent (s. 196(2)). Where harvest began before the plan's approval, its requirements are unaffected unless the plan says otherwise (s. 197(4)). The FSP and the forest development plan decide.

replant.note: Where harvest of a cutblock began under the forest development plan, its stocking standards stay in effect until the free growing stand is established and its site level information continues, unless the FSP says otherwise. The FSP and the forest development plan decide.

roads.note: A road the forest development plan included with its assessments completed is part of the plan considered approved; a road right of way under a road permit in effect at the plan's approval stays under the Code unless the plan says otherwise. The FSP and the forest development plan decide.

grazing.note: Sections 196 and 197 carry cutblocks, roads and their stocking standards from a forest development plan into the FSP; they set nothing on grazing.

terms.where: The forest stewardship plan's identified areas, and the forest development plan that included the cutblock or road
terms.holder: The plan's holder; the natural resource district
terms.channel: The holder, who must make the plan publicly available (FRPA s. 20.25(2)), or the district, by FSP and identified area id
terms.ask: The cutblock or road the area was identified for, the forest development plan and its completed assessments, and whether the minister found the unit inconsistent under FRPA s. 196(2)

instruments.label: Declared area of a forest stewardship plan (FPPR s. 14(4), repealed 1 January 2026)
instruments.note: As it read before its repeal, FPPR s. 14(4) let a plan identify as a declared area an area in a forest development unit in effect where every activity and evaluation needed to include cutblocks and roads in it had been completed (BC Laws point in time, read 27 November 2026). B.C. Reg. 163/2023 repealed it, with the definition, the deemed approval of s. 23, s. 30(1)'s amendment without approval and the protections of ss. 32.1(a) and 92.1(3)(e), effective 1 January 2026. The layer still holds the areas.

binds.note: Part of the plan its holders carry out. What standing a declared area keeps after 1 January 2026 is in B.C. Reg. 163/2023's transitional provisions, which were not read.

harvest.note: Until 1 January 2026 a declared area was within the plan's deemed approval, was left out of the mandatory amendments for a new objective, and was unaffected by an exemption granted for an established objective. Those provisions are repealed; whether harvest planned there keeps that standing is in the amending regulation and the plan, which decide.

replant.note: The plan's stocking standards apply as in the rest of its unit; the declared area's own standing after the repeal is in the amending regulation and the plan, which decide.

roads.note: A declared area was identified for the roads, as well as the cutblocks, whose activities and evaluations were complete; whether a road planned there keeps that standing after the repeal is in the amending regulation and the plan, which decide.

grazing.note: A declared area was about including cutblocks and roads in a forest development unit; it set nothing on grazing.

terms.where: The forest stewardship plan's declared areas, and B.C. Reg. 163/2023 with its transitional provisions
terms.holder: The plan's holder; the natural resource district
terms.channel: The holder, who must make the plan publicly available (FRPA s. 20.25(2)), or the district, by FSP and identified area id
terms.ask: The cutblocks and roads the area was declared for, whether a permit was issued for them before 1 January 2026, and how the district treats the area since the declared area provisions were repealed
